book.title: 拼音王国里的小弯钩
book.subtitle: b 和 d 怎么又转晕啦？

moral.zh: 刚学新符号分不清很正常；把身体当成小尺子，多试几次就能找到方向。
moral.en: It is normal to confuse new symbols at first; using our hands and body makes finding the way fun and clear.

pages.zhText: 大班的阅读角新添了彩色拼音图卡。安安觉得红红绿绿的小符号，像坐上小火车的乘客，想凑近看看。
pages.enText: New pinyin picture cards appeared in the kindergarten reading corner. Their colorful shapes reminded An'an of little train passengers. She wanted a closer look.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Bright classroom wall view: colorful chart with abstract rounded pinyin shapes on cork board; wooden desks and daylight from window.
pages.generationPrompt: Bright classroom wall view: colorful chart with abstract rounded pinyin shapes on cork board; wooden desks and daylight from window.

pages.zhText: 安安对两个相像的符号感兴趣。林老师陪她念：“右下半圆 b，左下半圆 d。”旁边的小朋友也来看看。
pages.enText: Two similar shapes caught An'an's interest. Teacher Lin joined her: “The loop is on the right in b, and on the left in d.” Other children came to look.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Classroom front view: Teacher Lin points to wooden pointer near chart; children sitting at desks chanting together.

pages.zhText: 安安想照着图卡画一画。她拿起铅笔，看着四线三格纸：竖线直直的，可圆圈该画在哪一边呢？
pages.enText: An'an wanted to try copying the shapes. She picked up a pencil and looked at the lined paper. The stem was straight, but which side needed the loop?
pages.illustrationPrompt: Desk close-up: An'an holds yellow pencil above blank lined notebook, brow furrowed in deep thought; yellow star clip visible.

pages.zhText: 安安盯着本子看了半天，小脑袋歪向左边，又歪向右边。两个字母在脑子里转来转去，像转动的小陀螺。
pages.enText: An'an stared at her notebook, tilting her head left and then right. The two letters seemed to spin inside her mind like little tops.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Medium desk view: An'an tilts head with puzzled expression, eraser in left hand, pencil poised in right, blank lines on open book.

pages.zhText: 她一笔画下去，把圆圈画在了左边，可心里又觉得不对。拿橡皮擦掉，重新画在右边，怎么看还是觉得别扭。
pages.enText: She drew a circle on the left, but felt it was wrong. She erased it and drew it on the right, still feeling unsure.

pages.zhText: 旁边的小宇以前玩过这些图卡，已经画了一行。安安看看他的纸，再看看自己的，心里开始着急。
pages.enText: Xiaoyu had played with these cards before and had drawn a whole row. An'an looked from his paper to hers and began to worry.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Two-desk view: Xiaoyu in forest-green sweatshirt writes smoothly; An'an glances sideways at his notebook with a worried sigh.

pages.zhText: 安安急得吸了吸鼻子，手心开始冒出汗水。用力一擦，本子上的格子线被擦得模模糊糊，铅笔尖也“啪”的一声断掉了。
pages.enText: An'an grew anxious, her palms turning sweaty. She rubbed too hard, smudging the lines until her pencil lead snapped with a tiny snap.

pages.zhText: 安安吸了吸泛酸的鼻子，把头埋进手臂里，眼泪一滴滴落在了桌面上。“我怎么总分不清呢……”她小声吸泣。
pages.enText: An'an sniffled, burying her face in her arms as a tear slipped onto the oak desk. “Why do I always mix them up?” she sobbed softly.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Side view: An'an rests head on arms across desk, shoulders shaking slightly; notebook pushed aside, broken pencil nearby.

pages.enText: Teacher Lin came over. “Mixing them up feels frustrating, doesn't it? Shall we rest on the mat?” An'an nodded and sat beside her.

pages.enText: The teacher offered a tissue. “New shapes can be easy to mix up. You do not have to keep up with anyone. We can try looking another way.”
pages.illustrationPrompt: Close two-person conversation: Teacher Lin dabs An'an's cheek gently; An'an looks up, listening with reddened nose.

pages.enText: First, they moved their hands. “Make a fist, then let go. Give your fingers a rest.” As An'an copied her, her shoulders began to relax too.

pages.enText: Sitting beside An'an and facing the same way, the teacher turned her palms toward herself and raised her thumbs. “From this view, the left fist has its loop left of the stem, like d.”

pages.enText: “With palms toward you, the left hand looks like d and the right like b,” the teacher said. “Turning them changes the view, so check the cards too.” An'an nodded.

pages.enText: Lele and Xiaoyu joined them. They checked the cards and gently moved their hands: “Loop on the right, b. Loop on the left, d.” A mix-up simply meant another look.

pages.enText: This time, the loops faced the right way. An'an smiled. If they confused her again, she could pause, check a card, and try once more.

pages.enText: At dismissal, An'an showed Mom her notebook stamped with little stars: “Mom, my two hands learned a magical pinyin trick today!”

parentGuide.goal: 将抽象的拼音符号与具象身体动作连接，化解大班幼小衔接中的认读混淆与挫败感。
parentGuide.reminder: 拼音是孩子感兴趣时的图卡游戏，不是大班必学、必写或入学测评要求。手势须成人与孩子同向，并明确手心朝自己；变换视角会镜像，不适合时直接看图卡。不要催写、比较速度或贴“笨、粗心”的标签。
questions: 图卡上的 b 和 d，圆圈分别在哪一边？
看自己的小手时，为什么要先说好手心朝哪边？
parentGuide.activity: 成人先与孩子并排坐、朝同一方向，把手心朝自己、握拳竖拇指，再对照 b、d 图卡观察。孩子不喜欢或觉得更混淆时就停下，用图卡找相同形状即可，不要求书写或背诵。

ageTips.age4to5: 允许孩子用指图、点头、手势等非语言方式表达；共读以倾听、感受安抚为主，不强求马上做到。
ageTips.age6to8: 讨论大班一日生活中的真实感受与解决策略，鼓励孩子自己提出小行动，家长承担托底支持与陪伴责任。
